name: Tabal
native: Bit-Burutas (Assyrian name after the c. 718 reorganisation)

predecessors.name: Neo-Hittite states
predecessors.text: the Tabalian region, which the Neo-Hittite states page lists in the northern group: Kammanu (with Melid), Hilakku, Hiyawa, Gurgum, Kummuh and Carchemish

successors.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
successors.text: Tabal's land, an Assyrian province (Bit-Burutas) from 713

ledger.x: c. 738: Tabal becomes a tributary of Assyria. 'By c. 738 BC, the Tabalian region, including Tabal proper, had become a tributary of the Neo-Assyrian king' (infobox 'Submission to the Neo-Assyrian Empire: c. 740 BC'; 'Vassal of the Neo-Assyrian Empire (c. 740s - 713 BC)'). Tabal is the vassal and neo-assyrian-empire…

c. 718: Tabal is reorganised into Bit-Burutas. Infobox 'Reorganisation into Bīt-Burutaš: c. 718 BC'; Sargon II restored Ḫullî in 721 and 'soon appointed Ḫullî's son Ambaris as his successor to the kingship of Tabal'. Same state, same colour.

wars.name: Shalmaneser III's Tabalian campaign
wars.outcome: Tuwattis I surrendered when the Assyrian army surrounded his city; the kings of Tabal offered tribute again in 836.

wars.name: Tiglath-pileser III's subjugation of Tabal
wars.outcome: By c. 738 the Tabalian region was a tributary of the Neo-Assyrian king; c. 732-730 Tiglath-pileser deposed Wasusarmas and installed Hulli.

wars.name: Sargon II's annexation of Bit-Burutas
wars.outcome: Ambaris, pressed by Midas of Phrygia from c.

certainty.note: No page gives a Tabalian border.
